theorem ConvexOn.map_sum_le (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1)
    (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)
declarations.doc: Convex **Jensen's inequality**, `Finset.sum` version.
declarations.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_4} {ι : Type u_5} [inst : LinearOrderedField.{u_1} 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommGroup.{u_2} E] [inst_2 : OrderedAddCommGroup.{u_4} β] [inst_3 : Module.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 E]
  [inst_4 : Module.{u_1, u_4} 𝕜 β] [inst_5 : OrderedSMul.{u_1, u_4} 𝕜 β] {s : Set.{u_2} E} {f : E → β}
  {t : Finset.{u_5} ι} {w : ι → 𝕜} {p : ι → E},
  ConvexOn.{u_1, u_2, u_4} 𝕜 s f →
    (∀ (i : ι), Membership.mem.{u_5, u_5} t i → LE.le.{u_1} 0 (w i)) →
      Eq.{u_1 + 1} (∑ i ∈ t, w i) 1 →
        (∀ (i : ι), Membership.mem.{u_5, u_5} t i → Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s (p i)) →
          LE.le.{u_4} (f (∑ i ∈ t, HSMul.hSMul.{u_1, u_2, u_2} (w i) (p i)))
            (∑ i ∈ t, HSMul.hSMul.{u_1, u_4, u_4} (w i) (f (p i)))

If the function is strictly convex, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of

declarations.name: ConvexOn.map_integral_le
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem ConvexOn.map_integral_le [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hg : ConvexOn ℝ s g)
    (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ)
    (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : g (∫ x, f x ∂μ) ≤ ∫ x, g (f x) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is convex and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a probability measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending `μ`-a.e.  points
to `s`, then the value of `g` at the expected value of `f` is less than or equal to the expected
value of `g ∘ f` provided that both `f` and `g ∘ f` are integrable. See also
`ConvexOn.map_centerMass_le` for a finite sum version of this lemma.
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_2} E]
  [inst_1 : NormedSpace.{0, u_2} Real E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace.{u_2} E] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α}
  {s : Set.{u_2} E} {f : α → E} {g : E → Real} [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_1} μ],
  ConvexOn.{0, u_2, 0} Real s g →
    ContinuousOn.{u_2, 0} g s →
      IsClosed.{u_2} s →
        (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s (f x)) →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable.{u_2, u_1} f μ →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} (Function.comp.{u_1 + 1, u_2 + 1, 1} g f) μ →
              LE.le.{0} (g (∫ (x : α), f x ∂μ)) (∫ (x : α), g (f x) ∂μ)

    (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hp : ∃ j ∈ t, ∃ k ∈ t, p j ≠ p k) :
    f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) < ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)
declarations.doc:
Convex **strict Jensen inequality**.

If the function is strictly convex, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of
points is non-constant, then Jensen's inequality is strict.

See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.

declarations.name: ConcaveOn.le_map_integral
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem ConcaveOn.le_map_integral [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hg : ConcaveOn ℝ s g)
    (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ)
    (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : (∫ x, g (f x) ∂μ) ≤ g (∫ x, f x ∂μ)
declarations.doc:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is concave and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a probability measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending `μ`-a.e.  points
to `s`, then the expected value of `g ∘ f` is less than or equal to the value of `g` at the expected
value of `f` provided that both `f` and `g ∘ f` are integrable.

    (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : g (∫ x, f x ∂μ) ≤ ∫ x, g (f x) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is convex and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a probability measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending `μ`-a.e.  points
to `s`, then the value of `g` at the expected value of `f` is less than or equal to the expected
value of `g ∘ f` provided that both `f` and `g ∘ f` are integrable. See also
`ConvexOn.map_centerMass_le` for a finite sum version of this lemma.

By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.lintegral_le_of_forall_fin_meas_trim_le
declarations.doc:
If the Lebesgue integral of a function is bounded by some constant on all sets with finite
measure in a sub-σ-algebra and the measure is σ-finite on that sub-σ-algebra, then the integral
over the whole space is bounded by that same constant.

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

Let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel and $
u \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ be a finite measure. Suppose that for all finite measures $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ with $\mu \ll 
u $, $D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$. Then the same is true without the absolute continuity hypothesis.

declarations.source_snippet:
theorem condDistrib_ae_eq_condexp (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    (fun a => (condDistrib Y X μ (X a) s).toReal) =ᵐ[μ] μ⟦Y ⁻¹' s|mβ.comap X⟧
declarations.doc:
For almost every `a : α`, the `condDistrib Y X μ` kernel applied to `X a` and a measurable set
`s` is equal to the conditional expectation of the indicator of `Y ⁻¹' s`.

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.condexp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib'

theorem condexp_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib' {Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup Ω] [NormedSpace ℝ Ω]
    [CompleteSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [BorelSpace Ω] [SecondCountableTopology Ω] {Y : α → Ω}
    (hX : Measurable X) (hY_int : Integrable Y μ) :
    μ[Y|mβ.comap X] =ᵐ[μ] fun a => ∫ y, y ∂condDistrib Y X μ (X a)
declarations.doc:
The conditional expectation of `Y` given `X` is almost everywhere equal to the integral
`∫ y, y ∂(condDistrib Y X μ (X a))`.

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

declarations.name: MeasureTheory.ae_le_of_forall_setIntegral_le
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {m0 : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α} {f g : α → Real},
  MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} f μ →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} g μ →
      (∀ (s : Set.{u_1} α),
          MeasurableSet.{u_1} s →
            LT.lt.{0} (μ s) Top.top.{0} → LE.le.{0} (∫ (x : α) in s, f x ∂μ) (∫ (x : α) in s, g x ∂μ)) →
        Filter.EventuallyLE.{u_1, 0} (MeasureTheory.ae.{u_1, u_1} μ) f g
declarations.conclusion: Filter.EventuallyLE.{u_1, 0} (MeasureTheory.ae.{u_1, u_1} μ) f g

declarations.name: ConvexOn.map_average_le
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_2} E]
  [inst_1 : NormedSpace.{0, u_2} Real E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace.{u_2} E] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α}
  {s : Set.{u_2} E} {f : α → E} {g : E → Real} [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure.{u_1} μ]

declarations.name: ConvexOn.exists_affine_le
declarations.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    Convex.{0, 0} Real s →
      ∃ c c',
        ∀ (x : Real), Membership.mem.{0, 0} s x → LE.le.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} c x) c') (f x)
declarations.conclusion: ∃ c c', ∀ (x : Real), Membership.mem.{0, 0} s x → LE.le.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} c x) c') (f x)
declarations.source_signature:
lemma exists_affine_le (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) (hs : Convex ℝ s) :
    ∃ c c', ∀ x ∈ s, c * x + c' ≤ f x

declarations.name: ConvexOn.affine_le_of_mem_interior
declarations.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    ∀ {x y : Real},
      Membership.mem.{0, 0} (interior.{0} s) x →
        Membership.mem.{0, 0} s y →
          LE.le.{0}
            (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) y)
              (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f x) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) x)))
            (f y)
declarations.conclusion:
LE.le.{0}
  (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) y)
    (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f x) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) x)))
  (f y)
declarations.source_signature:
lemma affine_le_of_mem_interior (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) {x y : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ interior s) (hy : y ∈ s) :
    rightDeriv f x * y + (f x - rightDeriv f x * x) ≤ f y

declarations.name: ConvexOn.map_integral_le
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem ConvexOn.map_integral_le [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hg : ConvexOn ℝ s g)
    (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ)
    (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : g (∫ x, f x ∂μ) ≤ ∫ x, g (f x) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is convex and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a probability measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending `μ`-a.e.  points
to `s`, then the value of `g` at the expected value of `f` is less than or equal to the expected
value of `g ∘ f` provided that both `f` and `g ∘ f` are integrable. See also
`ConvexOn.map_centerMass_le` for a finite sum version of this lemma.
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_2} E]
  [inst_1 : NormedSpace.{0, u_2} Real E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace.{u_2} E] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α}
  {s : Set.{u_2} E} {f : α → E} {g : E → Real} [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure.{u_1} μ],
  ConvexOn.{0, u_2, 0} Real s g →
    ContinuousOn.{u_2, 0} g s →
      IsClosed.{u_2} s →
        (∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s (f x)) →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable.{u_2, u_1} f μ →
            MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} (Function.comp.{u_1 + 1, u_2 + 1, 1} g f) μ →
              LE.le.{0} (g (∫ (x : α), f x ∂μ)) (∫ (x : α), g (f x) ∂μ)

theorem ConvexOn.map_sum_le (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 ≤ w i) (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1)
    (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)
declarations.doc: Convex **Jensen's inequality**, `Finset.sum` version.
declarations.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_4} {ι : Type u_5} [inst : LinearOrderedField.{u_1} 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommGroup.{u_2} E] [inst_2 : OrderedAddCommGroup.{u_4} β] [inst_3 : Module.{u_1, u_2} 𝕜 E]
  [inst_4 : Module.{u_1, u_4} 𝕜 β] [inst_5 : OrderedSMul.{u_1, u_4} 𝕜 β] {s : Set.{u_2} E} {f : E → β}
  {t : Finset.{u_5} ι} {w : ι → 𝕜} {p : ι → E},
  ConvexOn.{u_1, u_2, u_4} 𝕜 s f →
    (∀ (i : ι), Membership.mem.{u_5, u_5} t i → LE.le.{u_1} 0 (w i)) →
      Eq.{u_1 + 1} (∑ i ∈ t, w i) 1 →
        (∀ (i : ι), Membership.mem.{u_5, u_5} t i → Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s (p i)) →
          LE.le.{u_4} (f (∑ i ∈ t, HSMul.hSMul.{u_1, u_2, u_2} (w i) (p i)))
            (∑ i ∈ t, HSMul.hSMul.{u_1, u_4, u_4} (w i) (f (p i)))

declarations.name: ProbabilityTheory.condDistrib
declarations.source_snippet:
noncomputable irreducible_def condDistrib {_ : MeasurableSpace α} [MeasurableSpace β] (Y : α → Ω)
    (X : α → β) (μ : Measure α) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] : Kernel β Ω
declarations.doc:
**Regular conditional probability distribution**: kernel associated with the conditional
expectation of `Y` given `X`.
For almost all `a`, `condDistrib Y X μ` evaluated at `X a` and a measurable set `s` is equal to
the conditional expectation `μ⟦Y ⁻¹' s | mβ.comap X⟧ a`. It also satisfies the equality
`μ[(fun a => f (X a, Y a)) | mβ.comap X] =ᵐ[μ] fun a => ∫ y, f (X a, y) ∂(condDistrib Y X μ (X a))`
for all integrable functions `f`.

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

nodes.proof_hint: Mathlib lemma about absolute continuity under Measure.map, e.g. Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.map.

lemma exists_affine_le (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) (hs : Convex ℝ s) :

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

library_signatures.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    Convex.{0, 0} Real s →
      ∃ c c',
        ∀ (x : Real), Membership.mem.{0, 0} s x → LE.le.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} c x) c') (f x)
library_signatures.source_signature:
lemma exists_affine_le (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) (hs : Convex ℝ s) :
    ∃ c c', ∀ x ∈ s, c * x + c' ≤ f x

library_signatures.name: ConvexOn.affine_le_of_mem_interior
library_signatures.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    ∀ {x y : Real},
      Membership.mem.{0, 0} (interior.{0} s) x →
        Membership.mem.{0, 0} s y →
          LE.le.{0}
            (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) y)
              (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f x) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) x)))
            (f y)
library_signatures.source_signature:
lemma affine_le_of_mem_interior (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) {x y : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ interior s) (hy : y ∈ s) :
    rightDeriv f x * y + (f x - rightDeriv f x * x) ≤ f y

result.statement:
Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

references.statement:
Let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel and $
u \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ be a finite measure. Suppose that for all finite measures $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ with $\mu \ll 
u $, $D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$. Then the same is true without the absolute continuity hypothesis.

library_signatures.name: ConvexOn.exists_affine_le
library_signatures.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    Convex.{0, 0} Real s →
      ∃ c c',
        ∀ (x : Real), Membership.mem.{0, 0} s x → LE.le.{0} (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} c x) c') (f x)
library_signatures.source_signature:
lemma exists_affine_le (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) (hs : Convex ℝ s) :
    ∃ c c', ∀ x ∈ s, c * x + c' ≤ f x

library_signatures.name: ConvexOn.affine_le_of_mem_interior
library_signatures.type:
∀ {f : Real → Real} {s : Set.{0} Real},
  ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real s f →
    ∀ {x y : Real},
      Membership.mem.{0, 0} (interior.{0} s) x →
        Membership.mem.{0, 0} s y →
          LE.le.{0}
            (HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) y)
              (HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} (f x) (HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} (rightDeriv f x) x)))
            (f y)
library_signatures.source_signature:
lemma affine_le_of_mem_interior (hf : ConvexOn ℝ s f) {x y : ℝ} (hx : x ∈ interior s) (hy : y ∈ s) :
    rightDeriv f x * y + (f x - rightDeriv f x * x) ≤ f y

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

result.statement:
Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

Let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel and $
u \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ be a finite measure. Suppose that for all finite measures $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ with $\mu \ll 
u $, $D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$. Then the same is true without the absolute continuity hypothesis.

Let $\mu ,

u ) \le D_f(\mu ,

result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.

declarations.doc:
Conditional expectation of a function. It is defined as 0 if any one of the following conditions
is true:
- `m` is not a sub-σ-algebra of `m0`,
- `μ` is not σ-finite with respect to `m`,
- `f` is not integrable.

theorem ConvexOn.map_average_le [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [NeZero μ]
    (hg : ConvexOn ℝ s g) (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s)
    (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) :
    g (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ≤ ⨍ x, g (f x) ∂μ
declarations.doc:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is convex and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a finite non-zero measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending
`μ`-a.e. points to `s`, then the value of `g` at the average value of `f` is less than or equal to

    (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) : f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)

lemma StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i)
    (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hp : ∃ j ∈ t, ∃ k ∈ t, p j ≠ p k) :
    f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) < ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)
declarations.doc:
Convex **strict Jensen inequality**.

If the function is strictly convex, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of
points is non-constant, then Jensen's inequality is strict.

See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.

    (h_int : Integrable (fun x ↦ f ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal) ν) :
    fDiv f (μ.map g) (ν.map g) = ∫ x, f ((ν[fun x ↦ ((∂μ/∂ν) x).toReal | mβ.comap g]) x) ∂ν
declarations.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} {mα : MeasurableSpace.{u_1} α} {mβ : MeasurableSpace.{u_2} β}
  {μ ν : MeasureTheory.Measure.{u_1} α} {f : Real → Real} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure.{u_1} μ]
  [inst : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure.{u_1} ν],
  MeasureTheory.Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.{u_1} μ ν →
    ∀ {g : α → β},
      Measurable.{u_1, u_2} g →
        MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.{0, 0} f →
          ConvexOn.{0, 0, 0} Real (Set.Ici.{0} 0) f →
            ContinuousOn.{0, 0} f (Set.Ici.{0} 0) →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1}

                Eq.{1}
                  (ProbabilityTheory.fDiv.{u_2} f (MeasureTheory.Measure.map.{u_1, u_2} g μ)
                    (MeasureTheory.Measure.map.{u_1, u_2} g ν))
                  ↑(∫ (x : α),
                      f
                        (MeasureTheory.condexp.{u_1, 0} (MeasurableSpace.comap.{u_1, u_2} g mβ) ν
                          (fun x => ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_1} μ ν x)) x) ∂ν)

Eq.{1}
  (ProbabilityTheory.fDiv.{u_2} f (MeasureTheory.Measure.map.{u_1, u_2} g μ) (MeasureTheory.Measure.map.{u_1, u_2} g ν))
  ↑(∫ (x : α),
      f
        (MeasureTheory.condexp.{u_1, 0} (MeasurableSpace.comap.{u_1, u_2} g mβ) ν
          (fun x => ENNReal.toReal (MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv.{u_1} μ ν x)) x) ∂ν)

declarations.name: Convex.set_average_mem
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem Convex.set_average_mem (hs : Convex ℝ s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (h0 : μ t ≠ 0) (ht : μ t ≠ ∞)
    (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ.restrict t, f x ∈ s) (hfi : IntegrableOn f t μ) : (⨍ x in t, f x ∂μ) ∈ s
declarations.doc:
If `μ` is a non-zero finite measure on `α`, `s` is a convex closed set in `E`, and `f` is an
integrable function sending `μ`-a.e. points to `s`, then the average value of `f` belongs to `s`:
`⨍ x, f x ∂μ ∈ s`. See also `Convex.centerMass_mem` for a finite sum version of this lemma.

declarations.doc:
If `μ` is a non-zero finite measure on `α`, `s` is a convex closed set in `E`, and `f` is an
integrable function sending `μ`-a.e. points to `s`, then the average value of `f` belongs to `s`:
`⨍ x, f x ∂μ ∈ s`. See also `Convex.centerMass_mem` for a finite sum version of this lemma.

declarations.name: StrictConvex.ae_eq_const_or_average_mem_interior
declarations.source_snippet:
theorem StrictConvex.ae_eq_const_or_average_mem_interior [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hs : StrictConvex ℝ s)
    (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) :
    f =ᵐ[μ] const α (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∨ (⨍ x, f x ∂μ) ∈ interior s
declarations.doc:
If an integrable function `f : α → E` takes values in a strictly convex closed set `s`, then
either it is a.e. equal to its average value, or its average value belongs to the interior of
`s`.

Let $\mu , 
u \in \mathcal M (\mathcal X)$ be two finite measures and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable function. Then $D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) \le D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
result.proof:
By Lemma~ ef{lem:DPI_of_DPI_ac}, it is sufficient to prove the inequality with the additional hypothesis $\mu \ll 
u $ (hence also $g_* \mu \ll g_*
u $). In that case,  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _y f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(y) ight) \partial (g_* 
u )
& = \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} By Lemma~ ef{lem:rnDeriv_map_eq_condexp}, $
u $-almost everywhere,  egin{align*}   rac{d g_* \mu }{d g_* 
u }(g(x)) & = 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \:  . \end{align*} Using that expression, then Jensen’s inequality for the conditional expectation(Theorem~ ef{thm:condexp_jensen}), we get  egin{align*}  D_f(g_* \mu , g_* 
u ) & = \int _{x} f \left( 
u \left[ rac{d \mu }{d 
u } \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) ight) \partial 
u
& \le \int _{x} 
u \left[ f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u } ight) \mid g^* \mathcal Y ight](x) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} The integral of a conditional expectation is equal to the integral of the function, hence  egin{align*}  D_f(\kappa \circ \mu , \kappa \circ 
u ) & \le \int _{x} f \left(  rac{d \mu }{d 
u }(x) ight) \partial 
u \:  . \end{align*} This is equal to $D_f(\mu , 
u )$.
